plan: Full experiment design delivered as the nine required sections (a)–(i) above. Key calls baked in: ZB-1p≡ZB-H1, ZB-2p≡ZB-H2 (Qi et al. / DeepSpeed naming, one- and two-stage weight-gradient deferral, justified by literature); M ∈ {2,4,8,12,16,24,32,48,64,128} with P ∈ {4,8,16} as the robustness axis; t_b/t_f ∈ {1,2,4} and v ∈ {2,4} are the sensitivity levers, ranked with t_b/t_f as the largest threat to the hypothesis; primary metric is end-to-end throughput Θ = B / T(M) with steady-state utilization U as a diagnostic; three quantitative decision rules (D1: Θ_ZB-2p(P) ≥ 0.9·Θ_ZB-2p(32P); D2: Θ_1F1B(16P)/Θ_1F1B(P) ≥ 2; D3 ordering among the four at M=P); closed forms for 1F1B and 1F1B-I plus a residual-bubble closed form for ZB-1p; ZB-2p falls to a 300-line pure-Python discrete-event simulator using only heapq/dataclasses/itertools; feasibility confirmed for the empty-repo, no-pip, no-network, CPU-only environment. Seven enumerated threats to validity, all listed with bias direction. The deliverable is design-only as per the contract; no simulation results are claimed.

context.question: Does the throughput for methods 1F1B, 1F1B-I, and ZB-1p improve as the number of microbatches increases, while ZB-2p maintains high throughput even with fewer microbatches? (Note: These methods are implemented as part of the zero bubble pipeline parallelism strategies in this repository, which aim to reduce pipeline bubbles and maintain high throughput.)
